properties.name: Río Tinto
properties.summary: Highly acidic, iron-rich river (mean pH 2.3) rising at Peña de Hierro in the Iberian Pyrite Belt and reaching the Atlantic at Huelva. Its ferric sulphates and iron oxides, including jarosite and hematite, make it a classic analogue for Meridiani Planum, Mars.
properties.target_feature: Meridiani Planum sulphate- and hematite-bearing outcrops (jarosite, hematite)
properties.science_relevance: Río Tinto precipitates jarosite, schwertmannite, goethite and hematite from acidic, iron-rich water, comparable to the jarosite and hematite identified at Meridiani Planum by Mössbauer spectroscopy. Its acidity is generated by chemolithotrophic micro-organisms oxidising subsurface pyrite, making it a model for iron- and sulphur-based habitability on Mars.
properties.analogue_limitations: Meridiani sediments formed in an arid aeolian and aqueous setting, whereas Tinto sediments form in seasonally arid stream beds; Tinto acidity comes from pyrite oxidation, which is not the only possible source of acidic fluids on Mars; ferric sulphates do not persist in the Tinto rock record, unlike Meridiani; the basin has more than 5,000 years of mining history.
properties.age: Iberian Pyrite Belt formed during the Hercynian orogeny; gossans older than 6 Ma; oldest river terrace dated to 2.1 Ma
properties.notable_organisms: Acidithiobacillus; Leptospirillum; Acidiphilium; Chlamydomonas; Dunaliella; Chlorella; Klebsormidium; Cyanidium; Euglena; pennate diatoms; Methanosaeta concilii (sediments)
properties.permit_authority: Junta de Andalucía (Consejería de Medio Ambiente), managing authority of the Paisaje Protegido de Río Tinto
properties.sampling_rules: Protected landscape (Decree 558/2004): access to publicly owned land only via designated, signposted places; the environment authority may restrict zones for research or conservation; aggregate extraction and actions altering the river's water character are prohibited; no specific sampling rules are set out in the decree.
properties.safety_notes: River water is around pH 2; avoid skin and eye contact and use gloves and eye protection when sampling. The basin contains extensive historical and active mine workings (copper production restarted in 2016).

references.citation: Amils, R., Fernández-Remolar, D. & the IPBSL Team (2014). Río Tinto: A Geochemical and Mineralogical Terrestrial Analogue of Mars. Life, 4(3), 511–534.

compare.why: Rio Tinto's acidic, iron-sulfate waters precipitate jarosite and hematite. Opportunity found the same pairing in the sulfate-rich outcrops and hematite 'blueberries' at Meridiani Planum.

properties.name: Atacama Desert – Yungay area
properties.region: Antofagasta Region, hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert
properties.summary: Hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert near Yungay, Chile. Its saline soils, rich in nitrates, sulphates and perchlorates and very poor in organics, hold extremely sparse microbial life. The site is a classic Mars soil analogue first proposed in 2003.
properties.target_feature: Hyperarid, oxidising, nitrate- and perchlorate-bearing soils with trace organics (dry limit of microbial life)
properties.science_relevance: Navarro-González et al. (2003) found Mars-like soils at Yungay: trace organics, very few culturable bacteria, no recoverable DNA, and non-biological decomposition of organics in Viking-style labelled-release experiments. Later work uses the site as an analogue for an incomplete nitrogen cycle on Mars and for the effect of rare floods on dry-adapted ecosystems.
properties.salinity: Highly saline soils enriched in nitrates, sulphates and perchlorates; halite and sodium nitrate identified by XRD in post-rain lagoons
properties.notable_organisms: Halomonas yungayensis (new species described from post-2017-rain lagoons); Halomonas, Marinimicrobium, Marinobacter, Acinetobacter dominate post-rain soils

references.citation: Navarro-González, R., Rainey, F. A., Molina, P., Bagaley, D. R., Hollen, B. J., de la Rosa, J., Small, A. M., Quinn, R. C., Grunthaner, F. properties.name: Dallol
properties.summary: Protovolcanic dome in the Danakil Depression, Ethiopia, where basaltic magma heats evaporites. The result is anoxic, hypersaline, iron-rich brines (pH down to -1.7, up to about 108 °C). The site is used to study the limits of life and iron mineralogy relevant to Mars.
properties.target_feature: Hyperacidic, hypersaline, iron-rich hydrothermal springs and brine pools precipitating jarosite-group minerals, akaganeite and hematite over halite
properties.science_relevance: Kotopoulou et al. (2019) describe Dallol as a Martian analogue where inorganic iron oxidation precipitates jarosite and akaganeite, minerals also identified on Mars. Belilla et al. (2019) found two physicochemical barriers to life where liquid water is present: chaotropic Mg/Ca brines, and pH around 0 combined with NaCl saturation. Diverse ultrasmall archaea occur only outside these conditions.
rock_types: Evaporites (halite-dominated salt deposits, potash) over basaltic magma
properties.age: Dallol volcano formed in phreatic eruptions in 1926. The last activity, possibly degassing, was in January 2011. The age of the hydrothermal system is unknown.
properties.salinity: Hypersaline: brines supersaturated in NaCl, with up to 150 g/L iron (mean about 22.5 g/L in spring brines). Mg/Ca-dominated chaotropic brines also occur.
properties.notable_organisms: Highly diverse ultrasmall archaea (including Nanohaloarchaea) in the surrounding salt plains and less extreme brines. No life was detected in the hyperacidic, hypersaline dome ponds.
properties.safety_notes: The UK FCDO (updated 7 October 2026) advises against all but essential travel to Afar, and against all travel within 20 km of the Eritrean border and within 50 km of Tigray. It reports renewed clashes in parts of Afar. Foreign nationals currently cannot fly into Afar airports, and medical facilities outside Addis Ababa are extremely limited. Fumaroles emit CO2, H2S and SO2. Brines reach about 108 °C and pH below 0.

references.citation: Belilla, J., Moreira, D., Jardillier, L., Reboul, G., Benzerara, K., López-García, J. M., Bertolino, P., López-Archilla, A. I. & López-García, P. (2019). Hyperdiverse archaea near life limits at the polyextreme geothermal Dallol area. Nature Ecology & Evolution, 3(11), 1552–1561.

Kotopoulou, E., Delgado Huertas, A., García-Ruiz, J. M., Domínguez-Vera, J. M., López-García, J. M., Guerra-Tschuschke, I. & Rull, F. (2019). A polyextreme hydrothermal system controlled by iron: the case of Dallol at the Afar Triangle. ACS Earth and Space Chemistry, 3(1), 90–99.

compare.why: Dallol's hyper-acidic, chloride- and iron-rich fluids precipitate jarosite and akaganeite together. Curiosity's CheMin found that rare pairing in Vera Rubin ridge mudstones, attributed to very acidic (pH ~1.4–2), saline diagenetic fluids.

properties.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
properties.region: Victoria Land, East Antarctica (between the East Antarctic Ice Sheet and McMurdo Sound/Ross Sea)
properties.summary: About 4,500 km2 of mostly ice-free valleys in Victoria Land: a cold, extremely arid, windy polar desert of valleys, ice-covered lakes and permafrost soils. A long-standing Mars analogue (used by NASA since Viking) and home of cryptoendolithic microbial communities living inside rocks.
properties.target_feature: Cryptoendolithic communities in porous rocks; cold-desert soils, permafrost and ice-covered lakes
properties.science_relevance: The cold, extremely arid and windy climate is regarded as an analogue for contemporary Mars and ancient Earth. Cryptoendolithic lichens and microbes survive by growing between the crystals of porous rocks, a model for where life might persist near the surface of Mars. Microclimate zonation and geomorphic processes are used to interpret Martian landforms and climate change.
properties.analogue_limitations: Unlike Mars, the valleys have an oxygen-rich atmosphere, liquid water in summer (meltwater streams and lakes) and annual precipitation of around 100 mm; endolithic life is therefore not directly comparable with present-day Martian conditions.
rock_types: marble and calc-schist (Asgard Formation, Skelton Group)
granitoid plutons and dykes (Granite Harbour Intrusives)
properties.age: Basement metamorphic and intrusive rocks overlain by the Beacon Supergroup intruded by Jurassic Ferrar Dolerite; McMurdo Volcanic Group basalts 2.1–4.4 Ma
properties.salinity: Mostly fresh to saline ice-covered lakes; Lake Vida saline; Don Juan Pond the most saline water body
properties.notable_organisms: Cryptoendolithic lichens and photosynthetic bacteria inside porous rocks; microbial mats; cryoconite communities; anaerobic iron- and sulphur-based bacteria beneath Taylor Glacier
properties.permit_authority: Competent national authority of the expedition's Antarctic Treaty Party (e.g. UK: FCDO Polar Regions Department), under the Protocol on Environmental Protection; separate permits to enter ASPAs 123, 131, 138 and 154 inside the ASMA
properties.transport_notes: Access normally by helicopter from Ross Island, or over sea ice via New Harbor or Marble Point. Helicopters should use designated pads; overflight restrictions over ASPAs 123, 131 and 154. Vehicles restricted to lake ice or existing tracks unless specifically authorised.
properties.sampling_rules: Specimens (including rocks and fossils) only for scientific or associated educational purposes; collect only the minimum endolithic community sample needed for analysis; taking of native flora/fauna needs an Annex II permit; avoid trampling microbial mats (e.g. walk only on rocks at Boulder Pavement); follow ASMA zoning (Facilities, Tourism zone near Canada Glacier, Special Features).
properties.safety_notes: Strong katabatic winds: secure all equipment and supplies. Take extreme care with vehicles on lake ice to avoid rollover or breaking through. Spill kits and secondary containment required for fuel and chemicals. Record air temperatures range from 12.0 °C to −65.7 °C.

references.citation: Friedmann, E. I. (1982). Endolithic microorganisms in the Antarctic cold desert. Science, 215(4536), 1045–1053.
Marchant, D. R. & Head, J. W. (2007). Antarctic dry valleys: Microclimate zonation, variable geomorphic processes, and implications for assessing climate change on Mars. Icarus, 192(1), 187–222.

properties.name: Haughton impact structure
properties.summary: Well-preserved c. 23 km impact structure on Devon Island in the Canadian High Arctic polar desert. It is home to the Haughton-Mars Project research station and is used for Mars and Moon geology, astrobiology and exploration analogue work.
properties.target_feature: Crater-fill impact melt breccias; post-impact hydrothermal deposits; glacial and periglacial landforms and canyons (e.g. Astronaut Canyon, compared with a tributary of Ius Chasma on Mars)
properties.science_relevance: One of the best-preserved impact structures on Earth, in a cold, dry polar desert where weathering is slow. Heat from the impact melts drove a hydrothermal system that may have been a warm, wet microbial habitat, which makes it a model for impact-generated habitats on Mars. The site is also used to test habitats, spacesuits, rovers and drones for Moon and Mars missions.
properties.age: Impact c. 31 Ma (40Ar/39Ar weighted mean 31.04 ± 0.37 Ma; U-Pb lower intercept 31.8 ± 1.7 Ma; Erickson et al. 2021). An earlier estimate of c. 39 Ma (Osinski et al. 2005) is now superseded. Haughton Formation lake sediments are Miocene.
properties.permit_authority: Nunavut Research Institute (Scientific Research Licence); Qikiqtani Inuit Association (Access to Inuit Owned Lands Permit); Nunavut Impact Review Board (screening of land-based research); Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (Territorial Land Use Permit on Crown land); Mars Institute (written permission for non-Nunavut visitors to the HMP leased land)
properties.best_season: Summer (HMP field campaigns have run every summer since 1997)
properties.transport_notes: No road access. The HMP Research Station has a c. 200 m dirt airstrip, and ATVs are used locally. The Mars Institute asks visitors to contact it first to confirm the airstrip is clear, find out where experiments are running and learn the ATV trail routes.
properties.sampling_rules: A NRI Scientific Research Licence is needed for natural and physical science. Land-based research is screened by the NIRB. Archaeological and palaeontological sites need permits from GN Culture and Heritage. Access to Inuit Owned Land needs a permit from the designated Inuit organisation.
properties.safety_notes: Polar bears do reach field camps on Devon Island. Western University teams use electrified bear fencing around sleeping tents, set about a football field's distance from food, lab and toilet tents. They ban food and scented products from sleeping tents and carry shotguns and bear bangers. Report polar bear sightings to the local Government of Nunavut wildlife office.

properties.name: Iceland volcanic fields (Holuhraun and Krafla)
properties.region: North-east Iceland: Highlands north of Vatnajökull (Holuhraun) and Mývatn area (Krafla)
properties.summary: Young basaltic fissure-fed lava fields in Iceland's rift zone: the 2014–15 Holuhraun flow-field north of Vatnajökull and the Krafla caldera near Mývatn. They are used as analogues for young Martian volcanic terrains and for aqueous alteration of basalt.
properties.target_feature: The 2014–15 Holuhraun fissure-fed lava flow-field ('transitional' lavas, polygonal terrain, lava–water interaction); altered Icelandic basalts with smectite clays and other hydrous silicates; the Krafla caldera (c. 10 km) and its 90 km fissure zone
properties.science_relevance: Holuhraun is a large-volume, fissure-fed eruption used as an analogue for Elysium Planitia, the youngest volcanic terrain on Mars. Lava morphologies and fissure systems there point to similar extensional settings. Water-altered Icelandic basalts are used to test how well spectroscopic and XRD methods detect clay minerals, to help interpret Noachian aqueous environments on Mars.
rock_types: rhyolite (magma found at c. 2.1 km depth at Krafla)
properties.age: Holuhraun lava erupted 29 August 2014 – 27 February 2015; Krafla Fires eruptions 1975–1984
properties.permit_authority: Nature Conservation Agency of Iceland (Vatnajökull National Park)
properties.best_season: Summer. Highland roads usually open between late May and mid-July, depending on snow.
properties.transport_notes: Holuhraun is in the Askja & Herðubreiðarlindir area of Vatnajökull National Park and is reached by seasonal highland roads. Roads in conservation areas may stay closed until the area can take visitors even when the road is clear. Check road.is or call 1777 for current conditions. Krafla is in the Mývatn area of north Iceland.
properties.sampling_rules: Visitors may only go on the waymarked trail from the Holuhraun parking lot, and the thin lava crust is easily damaged. The park lists permits but the page gives no details, so ask the park office about research sampling.
properties.safety_notes: The Holuhraun lava is extremely rugged and difficult terrain, with a thin, fragile crust, so keep to the marked trail. Holuhraun was fed from the Bárðarbunga system, about 41 km to the south-west.

references.citation: Voigt, J. R. C., Hamilton, C. W., Keszthelyi, L. P., Varnam, M., Hibbard, S. M., & Stack, K. M. (2025). The 2014–2015 Holuhraun lava flow-field in Iceland as a planetary analog for young volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia, Mars. Planetary Science Journal, 6(4), 81.

properties.name: Pilbara Craton: Strelley Pool and Dresser formations
properties.summary: Paleoarchean rocks of the Pilbara Craton holding some of Earth's oldest stromatolites (Strelley Pool, c. 3.43 Ga) and c. 3.48 Ga hot-spring deposits (Dresser Formation). A key early-Earth and Mars biosignature analogue linked to Jezero crater studies.
properties.target_feature: c. 3.43 Ga stromatolites of the Strelley Pool Chert (seven morphotypes on a peritidal carbonate platform); c. 3.48 Ga geyserite and hot-spring sinter of the Dresser Formation
properties.science_relevance: Strelley Pool stromatolites are among the strongest evidence for life c. 3.43 Ga, and their morphology and environmental context are used to argue for biogenicity. Dresser Formation geyserite with stromatolites and palisade fabric suggests life in terrestrial hot springs c. 3.48 Ga, which the authors present as an analogue for seeking fossil life in ancient Martian hot springs. The Mount Ada Basalt and Strelley Pool rocks have been compared with the olivine-carbonate unit at Jezero crater.
properties.analogue_limitations: Rocks have been silicified, metamorphosed and deformed over >3 billion years; biogenicity of some structures (e.g. small conical forms) is disputed; Earth's Archean surface chemistry and plate-tectonic setting differ from Mars.
properties.age: Strelley Pool Chert c. 3.43 Ga (Paleoarchean); Dresser Formation c. 3.48 Ga
properties.notable_organisms: Fossil microbial communities only (stromatolites, microbial mat fabrics, inferred EPS with gas bubbles); no living analogue biota studied
properties.permit_authority: Geological Survey of Western Australia (fieldwork permits cited by Duda et al. 2016); native title and pastoral-lease holders may also need to be consulted (unconfirmed)
properties.nearest_town: Marble Bar (Strelley Pool is c. 34 km W on Six Mile Creek)
properties.best_season: Cooler months, June to August (mean daily maximum c. 27 °C at Marble Bar); avoid December–January (often >45 °C) and the December–March wet/cyclone season
properties.transport_notes: Remote: Marble Bar is 152 km SE of Port Hedland, and Strelley Pool is c. 34 km W of Marble Bar. Road conditions and 4WD needs not confirmed from an official source.
properties.sampling_rules: Fieldwork has required permits from the Geological Survey of Western Australia; Duda et al. (2016) inspected the Trendall locality outcrop without sampling it. Strelley Pool is classified by the National Trust and listed as an indicative place on the Register of the National Estate.
properties.safety_notes: Marble Bar holds the world record of 160 consecutive days at or above 37.8 °C, with a record high of 49.3 °C; cyclones can bring very heavy rain. Plan for heat, water and remote travel.

properties.name: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve, Shark Bay
properties.region: Gascoyne, Western Australia (Shark Bay World Heritage Area)
properties.summary: Hypersaline marine reserve in the Shark Bay World Heritage Area with the world's most diverse and abundant living marine stromatolites and microbial mats. A modern model for early-Earth microbial ecosystems and biosignatures.
properties.target_feature: Living marine stromatolites, microbialites and microbial mats (pustular, smooth and colloform mat types)
properties.science_relevance: Hamelin Pool's living stromatolites are modern counterparts of stromatolites found in the fossil record back to the Archean, so they serve as model systems for carbon cycling and microbial mat ecosystems. Metagenomics shows mats dominated by Proteobacteria and Cyanobacteria, with sulphate reducers and methanogens.
properties.analogue_limitations: Modern biota and an oxygenated atmosphere differ from Archean conditions; the sources opened do not discuss Mars directly, so the Mars link is indirect (via ancient stromatolite biosignatures).
properties.salinity: About twice normal seawater; 54.5–56 ppt at Spaven Province sampling sites (April 2014), with 66–88 ppt reported across the pool
properties.notable_organisms: Cyanobacteria (Entophysalis, Dichothrix, Scytonema); Proteobacteria; Desulfovibrionales (sulphate reducers); methanogenic Euryarchaeota (Methanobacteriales); Thaumarchaeota
properties.permit_authority: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA), Western Australia (conditional licence for scientific access); Australian Government environment department for sample export/collection (cited in Babilonia et al. 2018)
properties.nearest_town: Denham (c. 100 km NW); Overlander Roadhouse c. 35 km
properties.transport_notes: 27 km from the North West Coastal Highway via Shark Bay Road; sealed except a short 2WD-suitable unsealed section to the car park. 750 m return walk from the car park to the stromatolites.
properties.sampling_rules: Scientific access requires a conditional licence from DBCA. Walking below the high-water mark is not permitted; no swimming, snorkelling, diving or boating over stromatolites or within 300 m of shore; no fishing. Stay on the boardwalk/viewing area. Boardwalk closed since Cyclone Seroja damage; view from the temporary fence.
properties.safety_notes: DBCA advises planning your visit and carrying a personal locator beacon (PLB). Drones must follow CASA rules; never enter the water to retrieve one.

compare.why: Hamelin Pool's living stromatolites form along a shoreline. Jezero's carbonates line its ancient lakeshore in a 'bathtub ring' that NASA flags as a prime spot to look for stromatolite-like structures.

properties.name: Arkaroola
properties.summary: A 610 km² wilderness sanctuary in the northern Flinders Ranges, chosen by Mars Society Australia as its main Mars analogue research area. It has Neoproterozoic sediments and stromatolites, fossil hydrothermal systems (Mount Gee) and radioactive hot springs nearby (Paralana).
properties.target_feature: Fossil hydrothermal alteration and quartz-breccia systems in the Mount Painter Inlier (Mount Gee). Paralana radioactive hot springs with algal mats. Neoproterozoic stromatolites and ripple-laminated sandstones.
properties.science_relevance: Thomas & Walter (2002) used airborne and field short-wave infrared hyperspectral data to map hydrothermal alteration in the Mount Painter Inlier, as a test for characterising putative hydrothermal deposits on Mars. Mars Society Australia uses the area's varied rocks, regolith and duricrusts for remote-sensing, instrument and simulated-base testing.
rock_types: Neoproterozoic evaporitic, carbonate and clastic sediments (Callanna and Burra Groups)
iron, silica, carbonate and sulphate duricrusts
properties.age: Mesoproterozoic basement. Neoproterozoic sediments, including a stromatolite about 650 million years old. The main hydrothermal alteration is tentatively Permo-Carboniferous. Paralana springs are active today.
properties.notable_organisms: Algal mats on the floor of the Paralana hot springs in a high-radioactivity setting
properties.transport_notes: About 600–700 km north of Adelaide, roughly 8 hours by road. Charter flights are available from Adelaide airfields. The sanctuary offers guided 4WD tours (e.g. the Ridgetop tour) as well as self-drive tracks and bushwalking.
properties.safety_notes: Radon (heavier than air) is emitted at the Paralana hot springs, so prolonged stays near the springs may be a health hazard.

references.citation: Thomas, M. & Walter, M. R. (2002). Application of hyperspectral infrared analysis of hydrothermal alteration on Earth and Mars. Astrobiology, 2(3), 335–351.

properties.name: Lanzarote
alt_names: Lanzarote and Chinijo Islands UNESCO Global Geopark
properties.summary: Volcanic island in the Canary Islands with young lava fields (Timanfaya eruptions of 1730–1736 and 1824) and lava tubes. A Mars and Moon analogue used by ESA for PANGAEA astronaut geology training and for lava-tube astrobiology studies.
properties.target_feature: Martian and lunar volcanic terrains and lava tubes; interaction of volcanic activity and water
properties.science_relevance: Lanzarote has been described as one of the best terrestrial analogues for Martian volcanology, and its barren volcanic landscape is used by ESA to train astronauts in planetary field geology. Its lava tubes host secondary minerals and microbial communities whose biosignatures (e.g. Ca-rich fluorapatite precipitates) inform life-detection strategies for Martian caves.
properties.age: Geological processes active for more than 15 Ma; historical eruptions 1730–1736 and 1824 (Timanfaya)
properties.notable_organisms: Crossiella; halophilic and halotolerant chemoorganotrophic bacteria (lava tubes); Salinisphaera; Alcanivorax; Alicyclobacillus (La Corona lava tube); lichens (Timanfaya)
properties.permit_authority: Timanfaya National Park direction (Parques Nacionales de Canarias); Lanzarote and Chinijo Islands UNESCO Global Geopark / Cabildo de Lanzarote
properties.transport_notes: Timanfaya is reached by road (LZ-67 from Yaiza or Tinajo). Private vehicles may drive to Islote de Hilario (fee at the Taro gate); the Ruta de los Volcanes is only by Cabildo bus; guided walks (e.g. Termesana) must be booked in advance at the Mancha Blanca Visitor Centre.
properties.sampling_rules: In Timanfaya it is not permitted to walk or drive outside areas set up for public use (fragile lichens); plant collecting is prohibited; free independent access only on the coastal path; the Restricted Use Zone needs prior authorisation from the park direction; the Reserve Zone (over 90% of the park) is open only for scientific or management purposes.
properties.safety_notes: Timanfaya has geothermal anomalies with surface temperatures above 100 °C; about 277 °C has been recorded at 10 cm depth at Islote de Hilario. Keep to designated areas.

properties.name: Bockfjord Volcanic Complex
properties.region: Bockfjorden, Haakon VII Land, Spitsbergen, Svalbard
properties.summary: Quaternary basaltic volcanoes (Sverrefjell, Sigurdfjell) beside Bockfjorden, Svalbard. They contain carbonate globules like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001, with warm springs nearby. A long-running AMASE site for testing Mars instruments and astrobiology methods.
properties.target_feature: Dolomite–magnesite carbonate globules in mantle xenoliths and lava vesicles; vent-hosted magnesite and carbonate-cemented lava breccias; Jotun and Troll warm springs
properties.science_relevance: Carbonate globules at Sverrefjell show carbonate and iron-oxide zoning similar to those in ALH84001, so they help test low-temperature hydrothermal and abiotic carbon-synthesis models for the meteorite. Breccia cements at Sverrefjell are an analogue for the Comanche carbonates at Gusev crater. AMASE has used the complex to test MSL and ExoMars instruments and contamination protocols.
properties.age: Sverrefjell and Sigurdfjell formed in subglacial eruptions c. 1 Ma (Amundsen et al. 2011). Wikipedia gives Sverrefjellet's formation as c. 2.6 Ma, with a last eruption between 6 ka and 1 Ma.
properties.best_season: Summer (AMASE fieldwork has been in August)
properties.sampling_rules: Register every project and fieldwork location in the Research in Svalbard (RiS) database. Apply by the fixed deadlines (15 Jan, 1 Mar, 1 Jul, 1 Oct); processing takes up to 8 weeks, and fieldwork must not start before the Governor replies. Fieldwork in national parks usually needs an exemption from the Governor. Loose stones need no permit in principle, but the area's protection rules still apply. Fossil collecting in protected areas needs an application. Terrain interventions larger than 20 × 20 cm need permission. Pre-1946 cultural monuments are protected, with a 100 m zone. Work under the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.
properties.safety_notes: Polar bears: anyone outside settlements must carry suitable means of scaring off polar bears, and the Governor recommends a firearm. Campsites must be secured against bears, and camps that need an application must keep an awake, organised bear guard whenever people are present. Anyone travelling outside Management Area 10 must carry an emergency beacon registered with the Governor. Satellite phones cannot dial 112.

properties.name: Mauna Kea
properties.summary: Dormant shield volcano on Hawaiʻi Island whose fine-grained volcanic slopes hosted the 2010 and 2012 ILSO-ISRU field tests (PISCES, NASA, CSA, DLR, NORCAT) as a lunar and Mars analogue for instruments and resource extraction.
properties.target_feature: Fine-grained volcanic material and cinder-cone slopes (e.g. Puʻu Hiwahine, c. 2800 m) used for excavation, site preparation, mobility and ISRU instrument tests
properties.science_relevance: Mauna Kea hosted the 2010 ILSO-ISRU campaign, in which eight science teams tested and calibrated lunar in-situ instruments, and a 2012 follow-up under PISCES. Its fine-grained volcanic material is described as a suitable lunar and Martian analogue, and the site was proposed as a standard calibration location.
properties.analogue_limitations: An atmosphere, water and weathering make the material and conditions unlike the airless lunar surface; access and activities are limited by cultural, environmental and astronomical constraints.
properties.age: Volcano c. 1 million years old; oldest dated rock c. 237,000 years (±31,000)
properties.permit_authority: University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo Center for Maunakea Stewardship (formerly Office of Maunakea Management); Maunakea Stewardship and Oversight Authority (taking over management, transition from 1 July 2023)
properties.transport_notes: Saddle Road crosses the plateau between Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa. The summit road climbs nearly 5,000 ft over eight miles from the Visitor Information Station (2,804 m); it is unpaved, steep and requires dependable 4WD with low range above the VIS. No public fuel; arrive with at least half a tank. Summit open from 30 min before sunrise to 30 min after sunset.
properties.sampling_rules: Do not move, remove, collect or leave anything, including rocks. Rock piles may be cultural altars or markers protected by law. Stay on marked trails and roads; no off-road driving. Vehicles must be clean and free of invasive species.
properties.safety_notes: Acclimatise at least 30 minutes at the VIS (2,804 m) before going higher; descend immediately with altitude-illness symptoms. Children under 13, pregnant people, anyone who dived in the previous 24 hours or has heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions should not go above the VIS. Drink c. 500 ml per hour. Winter storms bring freezing temperatures, winds over 100 mph and white-outs. Intense UV. Mobile phones are for emergencies only; help may be hours away.

properties.name: Boulby Mine
properties.summary: Working potash and polyhalite mine on the North Yorkshire coast hosting the STFC Boulby Underground Laboratory 1.1 km below ground in ~250-million-year-old Zechstein evaporites. Used for Mars-analogue instrument testing (MINAR) and deep subsurface brine habitability studies.
properties.science_relevance: The MINAR programme used Boulby's Permian evaporite sequence to test a planetary instrument suite (camera emulators, Raman, handheld XRD, drills) for characterising geological context and mineralogy at millimetre to metre scales. Subsurface brines in the mine show how ionic strength and water activity limit life, relevant to potentially habitable Martian brines.
properties.analogue_limitations: Active commercial mine with engineered roadways, air conditioning and human contamination; brines examined were not extreme in ionic strength.
properties.salinity: Brine ionic strength 5.32–6.56 mol/L; Cl⁻ 159,347–209,639 mg/L; water activity 0.566–0.742
properties.notable_organisms: Halobacteriales archaea (Haloarcula, Natronomonas, Halogeometricum, Halomicrobium, Halobacterium); Proteobacteria; Bacteroidetes; Firmicutes
properties.permit_authority: STFC Boulby Underground Laboratory (with ICL-UK, mine operator)
properties.transport_notes: Surface facilities lie just south-east of Boulby village, about 4.3 km east of Loftus, between Saltburn and Whitby. The laboratory is about 1,100 m underground in an operating mine.
properties.sampling_rules: Access only by arrangement with the Boulby Underground Laboratory (contact the lab to discuss facility access); no public access.

properties.name: Lost City Hydrothermal Field
properties.region: Southern wall of the Atlantis Massif, near the intersection of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the Atlantis Fracture Zone, North Atlantic (~30°N)
properties.summary: Off-axis, serpentinite-hosted vent field at 750–900 m depth on the Atlantis Massif with carbonate–brucite chimneys up to 60 m tall venting warm (40–90 °C), highly alkaline (pH 9–11), H2- and CH4-rich fluids. A leading analogue for icy-moon seafloor hydrothermal systems.
properties.target_feature: Carbonate–brucite chimneys venting alkaline hydrogen- and methane-rich fluids from serpentinisation of mantle peridotite
properties.science_relevance: Venting is driven by serpentinisation, reactions between seawater and mantle peridotite that need only olivine-bearing rock and water and produce H2 and CH4. Comparable systems could exist on the seafloors of ocean worlds such as Enceladus and Europa. Methane-cycling archaea in the chimney interiors show that such systems can support chemosynthetic life without magmatic heat.
properties.analogue_limitations: Lost City sits in oxygenated Earth seawater and hosts macrofauna and photosynthesis-derived organic input from above, unlike the oceans of icy moons. Its ocean chemistry, pressure and rock compositions differ from those inferred for Enceladus or Europa.
properties.age: Hosted on ~1.5 Myr-old crust ~15 km from the spreading axis; venting for more than 120,000 years (radiocarbon dating of the oldest chimney deposits)
properties.notable_organisms: Methane-cycling archaea (Methanosarcinales-like, ANME-1) in warm porous chimney interiors; anaerobic thermophiles; Bacillota and Pseudomonadota bacteria; diverse macrofauna but without the high chemosynthetic biomass of black-smoker fields
properties.transport_notes: Accessible only by ocean-going research vessel with remotely operated vehicles or crewed submersible (e.g. the 2005 NOAA expedition used ROVs Argus and Hercules from NOAA Ship Ronald H. Brown, with live video relayed to shore). Discovered in 2000.
properties.safety_notes: Visitors work aboard a research vessel in the open North Atlantic far from land; all seafloor work is by ROV or submersible.

properties.name: Lake Vostok
properties.region: Beneath Vostok Station, central East Antarctic Ice Sheet
properties.summary: Antarctica's largest known subglacial lake (~250 × 50 km) under ~3.7–4 km of ice beneath Russia's Vostok Station. Accretion ice frozen from lake water contains microbes, making it a key analogue for ice-covered oceans on Europa and Enceladus.
properties.target_feature: Subglacial lake water and accretion ice refrozen onto the base of the ice sheet
properties.science_relevance: Lake Vostok is a liquid-water body sealed under kilometres of ice under high pressure (~350 atm), at about −3 °C and in permanent darkness, comparable to the ice-covered oceans of Europa and Enceladus. Microbes in accretion ice indicate the lake may support life that must rely on chemical energy, informing life-detection and clean-sampling strategies for icy moons.
properties.analogue_limitations: The lake water has not been sampled cleanly; all biological evidence so far comes from accretion ice or borehole-frozen water, and contamination by drilling fluid is disputed. Ice cover (~4 km) is much thinner than predicted for Europa's shell, and the lake is oxygenated from air hydrates in melting glacier ice.
properties.age: Lake sealed beneath ice c. 15 million years ago (estimates 15–25 Ma); overlying ice holds c. 400,000 years of climate record
properties.salinity: Freshwater (described as a deep freshwater lake at discovery)
properties.notable_organisms: Accretion-ice microbes at 2.8 × 10^3–3.6 × 10^4 cells/mL related to alpha- and beta-Proteobacteria and Actinomycetes; viable Gram-negative bacteria; thermophile-related sequences such as Hydrogenophilus thermoluteolus; unknown bacterial phylotypes (AF532061, w123-10). Life in the lake water itself is unconfirmed.
properties.permit_authority: Competent national authority of the expedition's Antarctic Treaty Party (e.g. UK: FCDO Polar Regions Department); station access only through the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute (Russia)
properties.transport_notes: Only reachable through Vostok Station (78.465°S, 106.837°E; 3,488 m), a year-round Russian station administered by the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute, historically supplied from Mirny Station; has a skiway. The lake surface lies ~4,000 m below the ice surface and was first reached by borehole on 6 February 2012.
properties.sampling_rules: Lake access only by deep borehole drilling. Clean-room facilities and a contaminant library are considered prerequisites for microbiological work; drilling stopped ~100 m above the lake in 1998 to avoid contamination. Antarctic Treaty permits required.
properties.safety_notes: Vostok Station holds the record low air temperature of −89.2 °C (mean annual about −55 °C). At 3,488 m, low oxygen causes headaches and nosebleeds and acclimatisation can take one to eight weeks. Extremely isolated, with about 30 staff in summer and 15 in winter.

properties.name: Lava Beds National Monument
properties.region: Modoc and Siskiyou Counties, California (northern flank of Medicine Lake volcano)
properties.summary: More than 780 basaltic lava tube caves; used to test how lunar lava tubes could be detected and how stable they are
properties.science_relevance: Basaltic lava tubes with skylights and roof collapses resembling lunar tubes. Used to model magnetic anomalies for mapping lunar tubes from the surface (Bell et al. 2022) and to test lunar tube stability models with measured geometry and rock strength (Theinat et al. 2019). NASA BRAILLE also uses the caves as a Mars astrobiology analogue.
properties.analogue_limitations: Terrestrial tubes are much smaller (~30 m) than proposed lunar tubes; Earth has an atmosphere and weathering.
properties.permit_authority: Free caving permit from the Visitor Center (white-nose syndrome prevention). Research permits: contact the monument. https://www.nps.gov/labe/planyourvisit/caving.htm
properties.nearest_town: Tulelake, California (services also in Tionesta, CA and Merrill, OR, c. 20–30 min from the Visitor Center)
properties.best_season: Late spring to autumn: summer highs average 24–27 °C (75–80 °F); the Medicine Lake Road approach is open only mid-June to October and some southern roads may close November to mid-May. Snow is possible in any month; the monument and campground are open all year.
properties.transport_notes: No public transport. About 1 hour from Klamath Falls, OR via OR 39, CA 161 and Hill Road; 1.5–2 hours from Weed, CA. Nearest airport Medford, OR (c. 2 hours). No fuel in the park; fill up in Klamath Falls, Merrill, Tulelake or Alturas. Limited mobile signal (some at the Visitor Center, which has WiFi). Winter: icy roads; FS 97, FS 49 and FS 10 may close.
properties.sampling_rules: Do not break formations or mark walls; ask the monument about research sampling permits.
properties.safety_notes: Low ceilings, uneven footing, steep stairs and drop-offs from collapsed tubes; risk of disorientation in complex caves. Wear a helmet, carry several lights, never go alone. Some caves closed; check the current list.

compare.area: Marius Hills hole (lava-tube skylight), Oceanus Procellarum
compare.why: NASA teams have tested lava-tube exploration methods in Lava Beds' caves for the Moon. The Marius Hills hole is the first-identified lunar skylight into a probable lava tube: about 65 m wide and 80–88 m deep.
